Team / Maya —

Quick summary up front: Syndicata is asking for our recommended Dedicated SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4) for a 12-month reserved commitment with a burstable component. They have three primary workloads:

- High-throughput embeddings and near-realtime enrichment (short contexts, lots of small requests).
- Mixed chat & summarization with mid-length context (2k–8k tokens typical).
- Episodic long-context summarization/search jobs (40k–64k) for analytics and compliance.

Attachments: syndicata_fleet_profile.csv (workload histogram), redwood_sku_cost_model_v2.xlsx (baseline cost curves).

Questions I want us to address in our recommendation:
1) Suggested reserve mix (percent split by SKU) that balances $/token vs latency SLOs.
2) Ops constraints (KV cache memory, slotting/tiling implications, canary plan).
3) Fallback strategy when H100 capacity is saturated (model variants / reduced context).
4) Quick pricing posture to propose to the customer so GTM can push back on ask-for-peak pricing.

Maya — feel free to add anything I missed. Kimberly/Rishi/Priyom, can you each send a short write-up by EOD with the tradeoffs and a 1-paragraph recommendation we can send to the customer? I think a succinct three-line recommendation will be easiest for the account team.

Thanks,

On 2028-04-01 09:12, Diego Fernandez wrote:
> Quick summary up front: Syndicata is asking for our recommended Dedicated SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4) for a 12-month reserved commitment with a burstable component.

High-level recommendation (TL;DR):
- Reserve baseline capacity on L4 for embeddings and low-latency microservices (approx 60% of committed slots). L4 gives the best $/token for short-context and can be quantized for many instruction and embeddings models.
- Reserve A100 (80GB where available) as the general-purpose pool for the majority of chat/summarization traffic (approx 30%). A100 provides a balance between memory and throughput for mid-length contexts and multi-concurrent streams.
- Reserve a small H100 pool (10%) as the long-context, heavy memory headroom lane for 40k+ jobs and large-batch analytics; configure as a reserved+burstable mix so we avoid paying H100 for steady-state unless needed.

Tradeoffs & operational notes:
- Memory headroom: L4 (typically 24–48GB effective after quantization) struggles as context grows beyond ~8–12k without aggressive quantization or offloading. Use L4 only when we can quantize to int8 and the model quality is acceptable.
- KV / prefix cache: The long-context jobs will depend on large KV caches. H100 offers the richest local RAM for KV caching per slot; A100 can also hold sizeable caches but plan for lower hit rates if the fleet is dominated by L4.
- Latency SLOs: For p95 chat SLOs <200ms we should prefer L4/A100 depending on model and batch size. H100 is higher cost and can serve lower QPS but with larger contexts.
- Fallthrough behavior: Configure automatic fallback to a shorter-context compatible model (or truncated context with a quality-regression alert) if H100 is unavailable. Prioritize returning a result with degraded context vs queueing indefinitely.

Quick cost sketch (order-of-magnitude):
- L4: best $/M tokens for short contexts; good for embeddings.
- A100: ~1.8–2.5x cost of L4 for mid-context generation but better concurrency for streaming.
- H100: ~3.5–4.5x L4 (but necessary for very large contexts and high-precision models).

I attached a simple snapshot of the cost model with sample splits (sizing_by_workload_tab). Will follow up with numbers by workload bucket.

Kim — good notes. A few pragmatic points from ops + pricing perspective: 

1) Recommended commit profile (proposed):
   - 60% L4 reserved slots (baseline embeddings & low-latency chat)
   - 30% A100 (80GB) reserved for general chat + mid-length summarization
   - 10% H100 reserved (or committed as a burstable pool) — use for 40k+ long-context analytics

2) Autoscale & burst plan:
   - Reserve the L4 baseline and allow burst to A100/H100 (ephemeral) when queue depth triggers and latency budgets allow.
   - Canary policy: 2-week canary with 5–10% traffic routed to H100 pool for validation; monitor quality regression against baseline prompt set.

3) Fallbacks & model variants:
   - Implement a model-mapping policy: if H100 unavailable, route to A100 with truncated context and an explicit header in response noting truncation. This keeps application-level behavior predictable.

4) Pricing posture: propose a blended commit with a 12-month term and a 15% discount on list for the blended mix above; include a defined overage rate and burst cap to prevent unexpected spend.

Ops implications (short): slot tiling and pre-warm latency for H100 are the biggest risks — H100 slot allocation can take longer to provision if we rely on ephemeral capacity. For this reason we should use H100 primarily for scheduled heavy jobs and reserve some headroom for quick-turn analytics.

Actionable ask: Diego/Kim, can we produce an expected $/1M tokens number for the proposed split (L4/A100/H100) and a 30-day pilot configuration (numbers + recommended canary). I'll push the pricing terms if we have the $ figures.

-rishi
